## Projects

### SaaS Churn Early-Warning System (Churn & Retention Analytics)
Page: https://www.aaryabhivsanee.com/projects/saas-churn-early-warning/
Code: https://github.com/aarya-7/Saas-retention-churn-early-warning
Tools: PostgreSQL, Tableau, Cohort retention analysis, Rule-based risk scoring

Aarya Bhivsanee built an early-warning system for SaaS customer churn using PostgreSQL and Tableau. HIGH and MEDIUM-risk accounts churned at about 17% a month versus 7% for LOW across 24 months, and retention fell from 90.1% at month 1 to 57.4% at month 6.

- Flagged who was about to leave: HIGH and MEDIUM-risk accounts churned at about 17% a month versus 7% for LOW across 24 months, using a rule-based score with reason codes (usage drop, errors, low CSAT, slow resolution).
- Showed where customers are lost: retention fell from 90.1% at month 1 to 57.4% at month 6 in PostgreSQL cohort curves, making onboarding the highest-leverage window.
- Caught churn getting worse: monthly logo churn rose from about 6% (May to Jul 2024) to 8 to 11% (Aug to Dec), lifting churned MRR to $400K to $500K a month, with 1–5 seat accounts losing about 18% of MRR a month.

### E-Commerce Funnel Diagnostics (Funnel & Conversion Analysis)
Page: https://www.aaryabhivsanee.com/projects/ecommerce-funnel-diagnostics/
Code: https://github.com/aarya-7/retail_rocket-funnel_analytics
Tools: PostgreSQL, Tableau, Sessionization, Window functions, A/B test design

Aarya Bhivsanee analysed 1,761,675 e-commerce sessions in PostgreSQL to find where the purchase funnel leaks. 97.8% of viewing sessions never reach cart, while 72.8% cart abandonment sits near the roughly 70% industry average, which pointed to the product page rather than checkout.

- Located the real leak: 97.8% of viewing sessions never reach cart, while 72.8% cart abandonment sits near the roughly 70% industry average, so the fix is the product page and add-to-cart step, not a checkout redesign.
- Found returning visitors converting at about 3x new visitors from 3 to 9 pm and several high-traffic categories below average, shaping 3 proposed A/B tests (product page, category UX, cart recovery).
- Built a PostgreSQL session mart (1,761,675 sessions; 30-minute sessionization, window functions) feeding 4 Tableau dashboards on funnel health, segmentation, category performance and time to convert, because aggregate metrics alone would have hidden the leak.

### GMV Anomaly Detection Pipeline (Anomaly Detection · Python)
Page: https://www.aaryabhivsanee.com/projects/gmv-anomaly-detection/
Code: https://github.com/aarya-7/gmv-narrator
Tools: PostgreSQL, Python, Claude API, Tableau

Aarya Bhivsanee built a revenue anomaly detector on MAD-based robust z-scores that surfaced 12 anomalies across 18 months and caught all 3 synthetic shocks. It flagged Black Friday as a +558% spike (z=29.79) and attributed 72% of that change to Southeast Brazil.

- Built an anomaly detector on MAD-based robust z-scores (less fooled by volatility than a standard-deviation threshold) over detrended GMV residuals, surfacing 12 revenue anomalies across 18 months with severity tiers, and validated it by catching all 3 synthetic shocks.
- Flagged Black Friday as a +558% spike (z=29.79) and attributed it to its drivers: 72% of the delta came from Southeast Brazil, so the spike was regional, not random.
- Automated the explanations: an LLM limited to precomputed fact packets writes What/Why/Action briefs where every number traces back to the data.

### H-1B LCA Disclosure Analytics Pipeline (Data Engineering · dbt/Snowflake)
Page: https://www.aaryabhivsanee.com/projects/h1b-lca-analytics-pipeline/
Code: https://github.com/aarya-7/h1b-lca-analytics-pipeline
Tools: Snowflake, dbt, SQL, ELT pipeline design

Aarya Bhivsanee built an ELT pipeline that loads U.S. Department of Labor H-1B LCA disclosure files into Snowflake and models them with dbt in RAW, staging, intermediate and marts layers, reconciling schema drift and normalising mixed wage units into one annualised figure.

- Built an ELT pipeline from raw DOL Excel/Parquet files into Snowflake, layered through dbt as RAW → staging → intermediate → marts, so every transformation is visible in version control, not patched silently in the warehouse.
- Reconciled real source inconsistencies explicitly in staging: a hyphen-vs-underscore column rename between Q1 and Q2–Q4, and nanosecond Unix timestamps cast to real dates.
- Normalized wages mixing Hour/Week/Bi-Weekly/Month/Year units into one annualized figure, flagging implausible values instead of silently guessing or dropping them.
- Deduplicated four quarters of FY2025 LCA disclosures down to one row per case, tracking H-1B sponsorship by employer, industry, and role across the NY/NJ tech market.

### Credit Card Fraud Detection (Applied ML · Fraud Detection)
Page: https://www.aaryabhivsanee.com/projects/credit-card-fraud-detection/
Code: https://github.com/aarya-7/Credit-Card-Fraud-Detection
Tools: Python, Random Forest, AdaBoost, XGBoost, Plotly

Aarya Bhivsanee benchmarked Random Forest, AdaBoost and XGBoost on highly imbalanced credit card transaction data, scored by ROC-AUC rather than accuracy. XGBoost led at 0.982, ahead of Random Forest (0.902) and AdaBoost (0.870).

- Benchmarked three classifiers — Random Forest, AdaBoost, and XGBoost — on highly imbalanced transaction data, evaluated by ROC-AUC rather than raw accuracy.
- XGBoost led at 0.982 ROC-AUC, outperforming Random Forest (0.902) and AdaBoost (0.870) at catching fraudulent transactions.
- Explored anonymized, PCA-transformed transaction features to find what separates fraud from legitimate activity without access to raw transaction meaning.
- Built interactive Plotly visualizations to make model results and class-imbalance tradeoffs inspectable, not just a single accuracy number.
